note: The board draws the launcher as issue 21 proposes it, not as it is today, and pins each issue to the control that has to exist for that design to be true. A pin whose anchor is not in the mockup fails the build, so the target and the issue list cannot drift apart silently.

issues.title: Redesign the launcher UI
issues.pin: This panel is the target. Today the same controls are one flat column with no grouping and no first step.

issues.title: Shared lobby URL with port claiming
issues.pin: The room code is the lobby, top right, and clicking it copies the link. Signalling, claims and the data channel all measured working. Last gap: a browser on a second network.

issues.title: Lobby replaces the mode list
issues.pin: One persistent room per URL, shipped: platforms/browser/lobby.mjs mints the room with replaceState and draws four port tiles. The mode links are gone. Nothing waits for a partner: the engine boots whatever the ports say, and a claim connects you into the game already running.

issues.title: Drop-in join
issues.pin: Taking a free port has to reach a match already running. Blocked, and not on the transport: the browser build defines no MELEE_STATE_SECTIONS, so snapshot_take() refuses every call and netplay is lockstep-only. See #34 and comment 2989 for the prerequisite order.

issues.title: Browser bypasses the lockstep guard
issues.pin: Why drop-in join is blocked: CMakeLists.txt:374 fails the build on a platform with no snapshot sections, and the browser target never reaches that check. Every online session silently degrades to lockstep.

issues.title: Spectators and the port queue
issues.pin: Past four players everybody watches and queues. Server side shipped: a release message frees a port and the first waiter still subscribed gets it, in claim order. The lobby does not draw the line yet; the place is a status string.

issues.title: TURN relay for symmetric NAT
issues.pin: The fallback this control names. Blocked: this network is cone, so it cannot produce the failing case.

issues.title: Modes become save states
issues.pin: Versus and Training stop being places to go. They load into the lobby that already exists, so nobody changes rooms.

issues.title: Verify the port runs on iOS Safari
issues.pin: The disc loads and boots. Measured working on iOS Safari.

issues.title: Flatten the web disc path
issues.pin: What the disc line is waiting on: HTTP Range over a 1.4 GB ISO. The engine reads files by name and fetches blocks on demand, so there is no load percentage; 60% of the disc is FMV that never plays. Gated on measuring the real working set.

issues.title: Disable Start while the disc loads
issues.pin: No disc load exists to wait on: remote-disc.mjs fetches one HTTP Range per block on demand. Start is already gated on a disc being present, at shell.mjs:176.

issues.title: Touch input layer
issues.pin: The shared state object every touch control writes to. One per port.

issues.title: Gamepad API for Bluetooth pads
issues.pin: A real pad claims a port like any other controller.

issues.title: Mobile CSS: pre-Start controls reachable
issues.pin: A test now fails if this bar moves out of thumb reach on a phone.

issues.title: Settings into tabs
issues.pin: Three tabs of five. Game, Video and Audio hold the settings that exist; Input and Netplay arrive with the controls in #28.

issues.title: 20XX as a select-all
issues.pin: Landed. The parent follows what env_flag_or_20xx reads: an untouched child follows 20XX, a child set by hand keeps its own value, and the URL carries a child only when it disagrees.

issues.title: Port the native launcher settings
issues.pin: UCF, aspect, HUD, textures, camera, stadium, volumes and the netplay name all exist in src/pc/launcher.cpp and on no web control.

issues.title: Training scenarios from a URL
issues.pin: Training is a state loaded into the lobby. Its tools run outside the player ports, so a scenario needs no seat.

issues.title: On-screen control layout
issues.pin: Where the pad layout is chosen. Needs a device in hand: no code decides where a thumb reaches.

issues.title: Accessibility defaults for touch
issues.pin: Tap-jump off, deadzone, curve, C-stick. Defaults chosen; the issue text still argues with itself. Wording only.

issues.title: Mobile layout: full-viewport canvas
issues.pin: The launcher fits this box with no page scroll. (pointer: coarse) and touch-action: none ship, and menu-button.mjs holds the controls. The launcher inside it is now #21's.

issues.title: Optimize the browser build
issues.pin: Measured on the phone: 960x720 holds 60 fps. The 17 fps reading was a cold shader cache, not the render size, so this control is headroom rather than a fix.

issues.title: Browser QoL: resume, pause, settings
issues.pin: Pause-on-blur landed. Resume after refresh and pause on crash did not. Parked.

issues.title: GC adapter called two missing C functions
issues.pin: Two calls into functions that were never defined. Removed.

issues.title: _malloc survived only by accident
issues.pin: Not in EXPORTED_FUNCTIONS. It worked until something else changed.

issues.title: launcher-close-repeat loses the GPU device
issues.pin: Apply reloads the page. Doing that repeatedly under the test harness destroys the GPU device on pass 1, so pass 2 finds none.

issues.title: Allow a CPU adapter behind a switch
issues.pin: A flag with no control, because it is for the test harness. aurora refuses a CPU adapter, so no browser check can boot the game.

issues.title: Headless runs can draw on the desktop
issues.pin: Fixed in melee-pc: the display variables are removed inside cage. melee-web still needs the same line.

issues.title: Condense the 20XX children into a closed grid
issues.pin: This fold, closed and two across. Unlock everything is drawn here as the target, but prefs.unlock_all has no env var, so it needs one line of C before a web control can follow 20XX.

issues.title: Controller connect belongs on the port
issues.pin: The WebHID picker is a page button today. A player connects a pad to the seat they are taking, so the control belongs here, with the source it feeds shown next to it.

issues.title: Signify which port is you
issues.pin: Closed. The tile you hold carries a left bar and the word 'you', because colour alone fails a colour-blind reader and a screenshot. The id moves with a claim and a release, and matching is on the server id, so two players with one display name still mark one tile. The spectator line below is the other half, and the queue on it is #23.

issues.title: Fill the Input tab, including controller options
issues.pin: The Input tab is drawn and empty: #26 shipped three tabs of five. Deadzone and curve describe a stick, not a seat, so this issue has to settle per-port against per-page first.

issues.title: Load button and save-state modal, instead of a disc chip
issues.pin: The chip read a percentage the browser build cannot measure. The slot becomes a press: Load opens the state menu, which holds the four presets and the states this player saved.
